subject: methRead no longer deleting uncompressed files after tabix compression

messages.author: f46993b38e0d7272
messages.subject: methRead no longer deleting uncompressed files after tabix compression
parts:
Hi methylKit team! Quick question - I recently moved to the newest version of R and the most recent Bioconductor release of methylKit, and when running methRead on processBismarkAln output, the uncompressed .txt file is not deleted after the .bgz and index files are created. As far as I can tell no data is lost in the newly created databases. This is unexpected as during my previous work using version 1.8.1, the .txts were deleted; I wanted to confirm if this is expected behavior. 


This can be replicated by using the vignette code as below: 

file.list=list( system.file("extdata", "test1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "test2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "control1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"), system.file("extdata", "control2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit") ) # read the files to a methylRawListDB object: myobjDB # and save in databases in folder methylDB myobjDB=methRead(file.list, sample.id=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"), assembly="hg18", treatment=c(1,1,0,0), context="CpG", dbtype = "tabix", dbdir = "methylDB" )

Thanks!!
Nia

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: methRead no longer deleting uncompressed files after tabix compression
parts:
Hi Nia, 

Thanks for pointing this out,  I think happens due to the two steps performed during processBismarkAln(): first methylation calls are extracted from the bam files and written to a file for each given context. Then these files are read using methRead to create the tabix file in the end, where normally the uncompressed file is directly removed. 
The reason why you still see those files in your folder is that the context in the filename of the methCall file is uppercase (i.e. CpG, CHH, CHG) and the context in the filename of the tabix file is lowercase (i.e. cpg, chh, chg). So the uncompressed version of the tabix file was actually removed, but the orginal methylation calls are still there. 

Best, 
Alex

messages.subject: Re: methRead no longer deleting uncompressed files after tabix compression
parts:
Hi Alex - thanks for the quick reply!

To clarify, the uncompressed file retained is from the methRead() function and created in the methylDB folder by default - I haven't noticed any unusual behavior from processBismarkAln(). I checked the filenames and they have identical capitalization - the output of methRead for one of my files is as follows:

methylDB/aMutCpG.txt
methylDB/aMutCpG.txt.bgz
methylDB/aMutCpG.txt.bgz.tbi

where in the past the first (.txt) file would have been removed after the command completed. None of the files, including processBismarkAln() output, have "cpg"-style capitalization. I checked the header of the uncompressed file and the capitalization is as expected: 

#Date:2021-01-25 07:16:31
#Class:methylRawDB
#DT:tabix
#SI:aMutCpG
#AS:b73
#CT:CpG
#RS:base
#NR:104118137
#DT:tabix
chr1    49      49      -       4       3       1

I hope this is clear and not more confusing than my first post!
